title: Satake data routed to the worker can come back changed, or never settle: restrictedBoard of E7 and E8 does not survive the worker wire
location: site/src/lib/worker.ts:138-145 (onmessage: p.resolve(deserialize(reply.result)) with no catch); site/src/lib/workerWire.ts serialize (a Board becomes { $board: specOf(board) }) and deserialize ($board rebuilt with resolveBoard)
claim: A Board inside a worker result is sent as its name or its matrix and rebuilt with resolveBoard on the main side. The 0-node board of a compact form cannot be rebuilt: the NotABoard thrown inside onmessage leaves the engineCall promise pending. A named restricted board whose matrix is in orbit order comes back as the standard board of that name.
expected: CONTRACTS 4: the worker message re-throws errors 'on the main side as the same class'. worker.ts header: 'a worker failure rejects the promise'. E-9: a call routed to the worker answers 'behind the same promise' with the same result it gives on the main thread.
observed: engineCall('restrictedBoard', [compact E8, black 1..8], { board: E8, kind: 'satake' }) goes to the worker, where whereToRun says 'worker'. The promise is still pending after 2 s, and the stub worker records an uncaught 'NotABoard: an adjacency matrix needs at least one node'. The same happens on the wire for e7(-133) and e8(-248). For e8(-24), main thread: rb.board has labels [4,3,2,1] and Cartan [[2,-1,0,0],[-1,2,-2,0],[0,-1,2,-1],[0,0,-1,2]]. Through the wire: labels [1,2,3,4] and Cartan [[2,-1,0,0],[-1,2,-1,0],[0,-2,2,-1],[0,0,-1,2]], so rb.board no longer agrees with rb.cartan. No reader reaches either effect today: T13 makes no call for a pair without a white node (MERGE ruling (4) on P6-A1) and never reads rb.board.
reproduction: From a clean checkout of f07eec6 plus this branch's files: npm ci; TMPDIR=<fresh dir> npx vitest run --project site-unit redteam-RT-03-p6-worker-wire (4 tests fail: E7 e7(-133), E8 e8(-24), E8 e8(-248), and the compact form through engineCall).
specRef: CONTRACTS.md 4 (worker message, serialization, 'errors re-thrown on the main side as the same class'); SPEC.md 5.1 E-9 item 3 (Satake data for E7 and E8 in the worker); RT-03 lens attack 22
proposedFix: Catch a deserialize failure in onmessage and reject the pending promise with it. Serialize a Board in a result with its matrix and labels, and its name, whenever it is not the standard board of its name. Either let a 0-node board round-trip or refuse it in the worker, so the error crosses as an error.

refute.citation: CONTRACTS.md 4 (worker.ts): 'Serialization: ... Board as its BoardSpec (rebuilt with resolveBoard); errors re-thrown on the main side as the same class.' CONTRACTS 4 state.ts: resolveBoard 'throws on not-a-board'. SPEC 5.1 E-9 item 3: 'Satake data (satake, satakeRecord, restrictedBoard) for E7 and E8' run 'in a Web Worker behind a promise'. The relabelling half follows the contract's own serialization. The never-settling promise has no text that permits it.
refute.evidence: Part (b), the named restricted board coming back as the standard board: CONTRACTS 4 prescribes exactly this round trip, and BoardSpec = string | { cartan; xy? } has no labels. It is also a logged and known consequence. DECISIONS.md:455 (P1-A2): 'a board { "$board": BoardSpec } (its name, or { cartan } from cartanNumbers) ... a sub-board's labels ... are not carried; noted'. DECISIONS.md:2247 (MERGE, phase 4): 'workerWire.ts serialises any named board by its name, so a board whose positions are not in its name's standard order (a folded board, later a restricted board of phase 6) would be rebuilt in the worker with its positions permuted ... a lead for RT-06 and P6-A1'. DECISIONS.md:3520 (MERGE on P6-A1) notes e8(-24) among the 7 named restricted boards whose matrix stays in orbit order. The finding's 'behind the same promise ... same result' is not E-9's wording, which reads 'behind a promise'; it comes from worker.ts's header comment. Part (a), the 0-node board: MERGE ruling (4) on P6-A1 (DECISIONS.md:3520) makes the restricted board of a compact form 'n 0'. resolveBoard refuses it. worker.ts:137 'if (reply.ok) p.resolve(deserialize(reply.result))' has no catch, and the entry is already deleted from pending at :136, so the throw escapes onmessage and the promise never settles. P1-A2's record says only 'A worker error event rejects every pending call', and worker.ts:5 says 'a worker failure rejects the promise'. No sentence permits a pending promise. Reachability: decisions/P6-A3.md:37 'A pair with no white node gets the empty restricted board without a call' (t13/load.ts noWhiteNode), so no reader reaches (a) through T13. This bears on severity only. Not in gate-G6.md open items. Not in the known-and-decided list.

title: Attack 29: restrictedBoard's board comes back from the worker as the canonical F4 (another position order and matrix) on E8 e8(-24), because workerWire sends a named board by its name alone
location: site/src/lib/workerWire.ts:62-64 (specOf: name whenever board.name is set) and the Board branch of serialize (:86-92); packages/engine/src/satake.ts:431-443 (the restricted board is named after identify() but keeps the orbit order, labels 4,3,2,1)
claim: On the E-9 worker path that phase 6 added for E7 and E8, restrictedBoard's board field does not match the main-thread result: the positions are in another order, with another matrix in position order.
expected: CONTRACTS 4: 'Board as its BoardSpec (rebuilt with resolveBoard)', and RestrictedBoard { ...; board: Board } (CONTRACTS 2). Attack 29: the worker path computes the same thing as the main thread, so the board must not come back 'with another matrix'.
observed: For e8(-24) (black 2,3,4,5), the direct call gives board.name 'F4' with cartan rows [[2,-1,0,0],[-1,2,-2,0],[0,-1,2,-1],[0,0,-1,2]] and labels [4,3,2,1]. Through engine.worker.ts's handleCall, the same call returns cartan [[2,-1,0,0],[-1,2,-1,0],[0,-2,2,-1],[0,0,-1,2]] and labels [1,2,3,4]. The other fields (orbits, simpleRestrictedRoots2, cartan, compositeWords) stay in the direct board's position order, so mapping an orbit to its label through rb.board gives a different label on the worker path. satake and matchCatalogue round-trip exactly for all 8 E7/E8 records. No visible effect today: T13 never reads rb.board (t13/model.ts:387 says the worker rebuilds it by name).
reproduction: From a clean checkout of f07eec6 plus the reproducer: npm ci --prefer-offline; node_modules/.bin/vitest run site/tests/unit/redteam-RT-06-p6-worker-satake.test.ts -t "restricted board that comes back" (needs no build; if Vite's SSR cache is stale, set TMPDIR to a fresh directory). 1 test fails with the diff above. The same file's 'E8 e8(-24): satake, restrictedBoard and matchCatalogue equal the direct call' fails on the same field.
specRef: CONTRACTS.md 4 (worker.ts serialisation) and 2 (RestrictedBoard.board); SPEC.md 5.1 E-9 rule 3 (restrictedBoard for E7 and E8 runs in the worker); RT-06 attack 29
proposedFix: In specOf, send { cartan } (with the labels, or a flag) unless the board's matrix and labels equal those of resolveBoard(name). Or have the engine name a restricted board only when its positions are in Bourbaki order, or build it in Bourbaki order.

refute.citation: R6: build-plan/reports/orchestrator/round-p6/out/RT-03.json, finding P6-RT-03-02 ('restrictedBoard of E7 and E8 does not survive the worker wire'), confirmed in this round: out/RT-03-reproduce.json reproduced true, out/RT-03-refute.json refuted false, TALLY.md 'RT-03 verdicts: ... 02 CONFIRMED minor'. TALLY.md also lists P6-RT-06-02 as 'DUPLICATE of P6-RT-03-02 (same cause, the wire's specOf)'. RED-TEAM-COMMON 5: 'One cause, one finding. If two findings share a cause, merge them.' Supporting R1: CONTRACTS.md 4 'Board as its BoardSpec (rebuilt with resolveBoard)', with BoardSpec = string | { cartan; xy? } (no labels). The wire format is logged at DECISIONS.md:455 (P1-A2: 'a board { "$board": BoardSpec } (its name, or { cartan } ...)'), and its consequence for phase 6 restricted boards is recorded at DECISIONS.md:2247 (MERGE, phase 4, 'Passed to the owner and later phases').
refute.evidence: Same cause, same location, same observed values. P6-RT-03-02's location is 'site/src/lib/workerWire.ts serialize (a Board becomes { $board: specOf(board) }) and deserialize ($board rebuilt with resolveBoard)'. Its claim includes 'A named restricted board whose matrix is in orbit order comes back as the standard board of that name'. Its observed gives, for e8(-24), main-thread labels [4,3,2,1] with Cartan [[2,-1,0,0],[-1,2,-2,0],[0,-1,2,-1],[0,0,-1,2]], and through the wire labels [1,2,3,4] with [[2,-1,0,0],[-1,2,-1,0],[0,-2,2,-1],[0,0,-1,2]]. These are exactly P6-RT-06-02's values. Its proposedFix also covers this case ('Serialize a Board in a result with its matrix and labels, and its name, whenever it is not the standard board of its name'). The RT-03 reproducer reproduced the e8(-24) values in two runs. At f07eec6, workerWire.ts:58-61 reads 'export function specOf(board) { return board.name !== undefined ? board.name : { cartan: cartanNumbers(board) }; }' and serialize sends { $board: specOf(value) }, as both findings say. Supporting records: SPEC 6.6 makes a type name ('E8') denote the standard board, and BoardSpec carries no labels, so the contract's round trip cannot keep a restricted board's labels [4,3,2,1] under either spec form. P1-A2 logged 'its name, or { cartan }'. MERGE phase 4 recorded that a restricted board of phase 6 'would be rebuilt in the worker with its positions permuted'. MERGE on P6-A1 (DECISIONS.md:3520) names e8(-24) among the 7 named restricted boards whose matrix stays in orbit order. t13/model.ts:387 says rb.board is never read ('the worker rebuilds it by name'). SPEC 5.1 E-9 item 3 says only that restrictedBoard for E7 and E8 runs 'in a Web Worker behind a promise'. Note on R6's wording: RT-VERIFY 5.3 names gate-G6.md or an earlier round's merge report as the record. Here the record is the same round's confirmed finding, which the harness pointed to and the tally marks as a duplicate. Dropping this finding loses nothing, because the fixer of P6-RT-03-02 receives the same cause and case.
refute.reason: R6: the cause (workerWire.ts specOf sends a named board by its name, so resolveBoard rebuilds e8(-24)'s restricted board as the standard F4) is already reported and confirmed in this round as P6-RT-03-02, with the same location, case and values, and one cause gets one finding (RED-TEAM-COMMON 5). The relabelling is also the round trip that CONTRACTS 4 prescribes for a Board, logged by P1-A2 and passed to the owner by MERGE in phase 4 (R1, supporting).
